instructions:
Write the issue the way Pxl, Paperboard's maintainer, wants to read it.

Title: one short, human sentence about what the user sees go wrong, naming the part it happens in. Not the cause, not an implementation detail.

BAD:  Missing await in supervisor restart handler
GOOD: Game Server panel says Stopped after the app restarts

Open the body with the problem in plain words, based on what the user said. Then name where it lives: the app (apps/paperboard), the server daemon (apps/daemon, or its Go supervisor in apps/daemon/supervisor), a panel by its name and id (like Blocks, dev.paperboard.blocks), PaperAPI, PaperUI, the docs site, or a service (Origami, Library, Arilink, Panel APIs). Say whether it looks like it only happens on one OS.

Then say what you found:

- The likely cause, with links to the exact lines at the commit you read.
- How sure you are, and why. Keep verified facts apart from your judgment.
- Steps to reproduce, if you know them.
- Whether the failure is shown to the user or swallowed. Paperboard should never fail silently, so a swallowed error is part of the bug.
- Anything that could lose user data or reach the user's .paperboard folder, called out first.
- Anything the maintainer should check that you couldn't.

Lead with the conclusion. Cite code, not guesses. No filler, no thanks, no headings for a two-line body. If you found nothing, say so plainly; a short honest issue beats a long wrong one. Don't propose a patch: describe the cause, and say if the part looks like it needs a rewrite rather than a fix.

If the report is a security problem (a page loading untrusted URLs directly, secrets stored in plain text, remote code running), say so in the first line of the body and keep exploit details out; point to the code instead.

Before you finish, check the title and body for secrets and private details (tokens, emails, home folder paths, hostnames, server addresses, Discord bot tokens, game server IPs) and remove them.
